title: Emrys and the Regiment
premise: In the winter of 1813, battlefield nurse Mara Dravenmoor has spent five years at the Harrowgate field hospital secretly recording the names of soldiers erased from regimental rolls—men written off as deserters or dead so their pay, pensions, and honors could be pocketed by Colonel Aldous Vane. When a gaunt stranger named Emrys arrives carrying a letter in the unmistakable handwriting of Corporal Thomas Wren, officially killed two years earlier, Mara realizes some of her ledger's 'dead' are alive, hidden in a shuttered government workshop where Vane forges documents. Together they must expose the fraud before Vane burns the workshop and its evidence—and before he silences the one witness who can identify every man he erased. The novel ends with Vane's court-martial, Mara choosing to publish her ledger rather than bury it, and Emrys, revealed as Wren's brother, finding belonging not in revenge but in the community of the remembered.
about_author: Xanthe Voss is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing military pension records and became obsessed with the gaps between official histories and lived ones. They write from a converted stable office in Yorkshire, surrounded by nineteenth-century ledgers and an ill-tempered cat named Quill.

chapters.title: The Ledger Beneath the Linens
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. At the Harrowgate field hospital, Mara tends the wounded while recording omitted names in a hidden ledger sewn into her apron lining. We learn her rules: which silences keep people safe. Emotional beat: weary vigilance—the cost of noticing what others are paid not to see.

chapters.title: A Stranger with Cold Hands
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. A half-frozen stranger, Emrys, collapses at the hospital gate clutching a letter addressed to him—in the handwriting of his brother Thomas Wren, listed dead two years past. Mara recognizes the name from her own ledger. Emotional beat: shock cracking open five years of careful numbness.

chapters.title: What the Rolls Omit
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Recovering, Emrys recounts how Thomas vanished after a battle, officially dead, no body returned. He shows Mara the letter: coded phrases about a 'workshop' and men 'kept writing.' Emotional beat: grief sharpening into purpose; two strangers realize they hold halves of one truth.

chapters.title: Colonel Vane's Kindness
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Colonel Aldous Vane visits the hospital, charming and generous, and Mara must smile while knowing—or suspecting—he is the architect of the erasures. She notices his aide copying patient lists. Emotional beat: dread; the predator walking calmly through the ward.

chapters.title: The Widow's Testimony
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Emrys tracks down a soldier's widow whose husband appears on no roll yet sends money home. Her fear of army reprisal reveals how deeply Vane's system runs—and that families know more than they dare say. Emotional beat: the quiet courage of the powerless.

chapters.title: Rules of Silence
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Mara's mentor, old Surgeon Brandt, warns her off: he once asked questions and lost a post. Flashback to her first erased name—a boy she'd promised to write to his mother. Emotional beat: the origin of her ledger; guilt transmuted into method.

chapters.title: The Workshop at Marlow Fen
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Following the letter's clues, Emrys locates a shuttered quartermaster depot at Marlow Fen where lights burn at night. He glimpses men in uniform doing clerical work under guard—faces he doesn't recognize until one turns: Thomas. Emotional beat: hope so sharp it hurts.

chapters.title: A Name in Fresh Ink
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Mara obtains a forged discharge document from a dying patient and matches its hand to letters signed by men officially dead. The forgery is flawless—official ink, official seals. Emotional beat: cold clarity; this is not corruption at the edges but an industry.

chapters.title: An Offer of Silence
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Vane privately offers Mara a promotion and passage home if she surrenders 'any personal papers'—he knows about the ledger. She refuses without confirming it exists. Emotional beat: terror held behind a steady face; the hunter knows she's hunted.

chapters.title: Brothers in the Dark
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Emrys smuggles himself toward the fen and speaks to Thomas through a fence at night. Thomas, coerced into forging his own death notice, begs Emrys to drop it—they'll kill him if Mara's ledger surfaces. Emotional beat: love weaponized against justice; the first fracture between the pair.

chapters.title: The Price of Noticing
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Surgeon Brandt dies suddenly—'fever'—the night after promising Mara testimony. Mara understands the warning. She copies the ledger and hides the original inside a coffin bound for England. Emotional beat: mourning fused with defiance; grief becomes ammunition.

chapters.title: Allies Among the Erased
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Emrys finds other survivors of Vane's scheme living under false names—a network of ghosts trading information. They distrust him but give him the workshop's schedule and the location of Vane's master book. Emotional beat: belonging among the discarded; the theme made flesh.

chapters.title: What Mara Keeps Safe
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Vane's aide searches Mara's quarters; she sacrifices decoy papers to protect the real ledger. A young nurse, Tilly, covers for her at terrible risk. Emotional beat: trust tested; Mara learns silence can protect as well as bury.

chapters.title: The Inspection
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. A visiting inspector arrives to audit Vane's regiment. Emrys attempts to reach him and is intercepted; Vane spins the audit into theater, parading healthy 'dead' men as proof of nothing amiss. Emotional beat: the law's blindness; justice outside the law begins to seem necessary.

chapters.title: Ashes in the Ward
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Vane orders the hospital's records room burned as a 'hygiene measure.' Mara saves a single box of true muster rolls at knife-point risk, aided by Tilly. Emotional beat: fury; the point where caution dies and resolve hardens.

chapters.title: The Plan at Marlow Fen
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Emrys, Mara, and the ghost-network plan to seize the master book during the workshop's quarterly supply run. Thomas agrees to leave a door unbarred—if Emrys promises his brother lives afterward. Emotional beat: fragile alliance; everyone wagering something irreplaceable.

chapters.title: Nineteen Names
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. On the eve of action, Mara reads her ledger aloud to the assembled survivors—every name, every mother, every pension stolen. Men weep; strangers become a regiment of their own. Emotional beat: the novel's heart; remembrance as resistance.

chapters.title: The Workshop Still Stands
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. The raid: fog, lanterns, the supply wagon as cover. They reach the master book as Vane arrives early and orders the workshop fired. Emrys finds Thomas trapped inside. Emotional beat: chaos and sacrifice; time running out becomes literal flame.

chapters.title: Out of the Fire
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Mara enters the burning workshop after Emrys; together they drag Thomas out as Vane escapes with a satchel—but the master book stays in their hands, scorched but legible. Emotional beat: triumph laced with loss; the workshop burns, the truth does not.

chapters.title: Vane's Last Ledger
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Cornered at the coast awaiting a bribed ship, Vane tries to buy the master book back, then draw a pistol. The ghost-network surrounds him; Thomas identifies him formally. Officers arrive—not to help Vane, but because Mara's copied pages reached London. Emotional beat: the law finally arriving where the powerless already stood.

chapters.title: The Court-Martial of Colonel Vane
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. At trial, Mara testifies with her ledger entered as evidence; Vane's counsel attacks her character, but the survivors testify one by one. Vane is convicted; the erased men are restored to the rolls. Emotional beat: justice within the law at last—but earned by everything outside it.

chapters.title: Every Name Read Aloud
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. Spring: Mara publishes the ledger rather than letting it rest in archives; Emrys and Thomas rebuild a cottage near Harrowgate; the ghost-network becomes a pension society. Mara, once defined by silence, reads the names publicly each year. Emotional beat: belonging found; power answered by memory.
